html:
Huancas is a label on the map for peoples of the central Andes of Peru. The best known are the Wanka, or Huanca, of the Mantaro valley, around today's Huancayo. The shape on the map spreads further north across the highlands and the eastern slopes.

The Wanka lived in walled hilltop towns and farmed potatoes and maize, and herded llamas. Around 1460, in the reign of Pachacuti, the Inca Empire conquered them and moved some of them to other provinces. The Mantaro valley became an important Inca food store on the royal road.

The Wanka resented Inca rule. When Francisco Pizarro came in 1533 they joined the Spanish and gave them soldiers and food. Their old language is a variety of Quechua, still spoken in the valley. Neighbours included the Chanka to the south and the peoples of Huaylas to the north.
